todaysEvents.summary: ADNOC tanker hit by missile in Hormuz
todaysEvents.delta: UAE's ADNOC confirmed a missile strike on one of its vessels transiting Hormuz Aug 8; 15 tankers targeted since Feb 28, three attacked this week alone with one crew member killed and 20 injured (Al Jazeera, Aug 8).

todaysEvents.summary: Iran sets steep demands to reopen Hormuz
todaysEvents.delta: Iran's Supreme National Security Council (Zolghadr) demands the US lift its naval blockade and sanctions, withdraw troops, pay reparations and release frozen assets before Hormuz reopens: 'until America corrects its behavior' (CNN/Al Jazeera, Aug 8).

todaysEvents.summary: Trump downgrades urgency on Hormuz talks
todaysEvents.delta: Iran's FM Araghchi says Tehran is not in direct US talks and wants compensation to reopen Hormuz; Trump calls talks 'semi-negotiating', citing Iran's inflation. Brent $84.35 (+1.0%), WTI $78.74 (+0.7%) (CNBC, Aug 10).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A signed Iran-Oman framework restores non-discriminatory, fee-free transit and traffic rebuilds gradually; Iran's Aug 8 demands - naval blockade lift, sanctions end, troop withdrawal, reparations, frozen-asset release - make a near-term signed deal unlikely (CNN, Aug 8). Brent moves toward $75-85 as the risk premium eases, while Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: No workable agreement emerges: Iran holds to its Aug 8 conditions, Hormuz traffic stays thin at just 8 confirmed crossings on Aug 7 (down 33% day-on-day, mostly via Iran's Unilateral Scheme), and ADNOC reports a third vessel attack this week with casualties (Middle East Eye/Al Jazeera, Aug 8). Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Iran's demands harden further, attacks on shipping escalate beyond this week's ADNOC casualties, and the Iran-Oman channel collapses, driving a renewed full closure of Hormuz and spillover into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu as Gulf cargoes become inaccessible.
